title: Asana MCP Server
summary: Let your coding agent read and update Asana tasks and projects through Asana's hosted V2 MCP server with a browser OAuth sign-in.
description: Asana hosts its own MCP server, so there is nothing to install. Point a client at the V2 endpoint and approve access with your Asana account. The agent can then look up tasks, create and update them, and summarize project status.
The older beta endpoint at /sse is being retired, so use the /v2/mcp address. Your client must support OAuth and Streamable HTTP transport.
useWhen: Turn the open to-do comments in the code into Asana tasks
Ask what is still open on this sprint's project
Mark a task done and leave a comment linking the merged change
Draft a weekly status from the project's recent activity

mcp.name: asana
access: Reads tasks, projects and comments in workspaces your Asana account belongs to
Can create and change tasks and projects

example.prompt: List my open tasks due this week in the Mobile Release project.
example.result: 3 tasks: "Fix push token refresh" (Wed), "Update store screenshots" (Thu), "Write release notes" (Fri). None are overdue.

faq.question: Why does my admin have to approve it?
faq.answer: On Enterprise plans, admins can allow or block each MCP client in app management. If sign-in is refused, ask them to allow your client.

faq.question: Does it need a client ID and secret?
faq.answer: Only if your client cannot create OAuth credentials itself. Asana's integration guide explains how to get them.

access: Asana tasks and projects your account can open
